intent: The single-line text field an InputGroup frames, drawn without chrome of its own.
typical_uses: The field of an InputGroup with a prefix, suffix or attached action

dont_use_when.situation: A single-line field with no InputGroup around it

invariants.text: `value` and `defaultValue` are both accepted; `defaultValue` seeds the initial state and is ignored afterwards, and when `value` is given it wins and the component follows it on every render.

Inside an InputGroup the field's own border, background, radius and focus or invalid ring are removed and it stretches to fill the row; its `:focus-visible`, `aria-invalid="true"` and `:disabled` states are what the surrounding group draws.

anti_patterns.do_instead: Put the icon or action in an InputGroupAddon; with a slot, Input wraps the field in a span that input-group.module.css does not lay out as the group's flexible field

a11y.by: input-group.test.tsx resolves the field by getByRole('textbox', { name: 'Amount' }) from its aria-label, and asserts that clicking an addon moves document.activeElement to it

icon.states: icon is a React node, not a value
icon.because: `ReactNode` is a union, and the compiler emits one JSON type per property - an element, a string, a fragment and `false` are all valid and only tsc can tell them from a mistake. It is Input's decorative leading slot, reaching this part unchanged.

end.states: end is a React node, not a value
end.because: `ReactNode` is a union, and the compiler emits one JSON type per property - an element, a string, a fragment and `false` are all valid and only tsc can tell them from a mistake. It is Input's live trailing slot, reaching this part unchanged.

value.states: value is the controlled field value, a string, a number or a readonly array of strings
value.because: React types a native input's value as this three-way union; the schema asserts nothing for it, so the TypeScript type is the statement and tsc is the checker.

defaultValue.states: defaultValue is the uncontrolled field's initial value, a string, a number or a readonly array of strings
defaultValue.because: React types a native input's value as this three-way union; the schema asserts nothing for it, so the TypeScript type is the statement and tsc is the checker.

onValueChange.states: onValueChange is a function called with the next value and event details, not a value
onValueChange.because: A function type has no JSON Schema representation. Its second argument carries Base UI's own change-event-details shape (a reason, the triggering native event, and controls to cancel the change or allow it to propagate), which only tsc can check.

render.states: render replaces the rendered element with one the caller supplies
render.because: Base UI's render prop takes an element or a function of the input's own state, so its type is a union of a React element and a callback - the compiler emits one JSON type per property.

style.states: style accepts a function of the input's state as well as a plain style object
style.because: Base UI widens React's `CSSProperties` to `CSSProperties | ((state) => CSSProperties)` so a caller can style off the primitive's own state (disabled, focused, filled, valid, ...). The compiler emits one JSON type per property, so nothing is asserted; the kit's own styling goes through input.module.css and input-group.module.css, not through this.

unexposed_parts.part: Input's presentational wrapper, icon and end spans
unexposed_parts.reason: InputGroupInput renders the kit's Input, which adds these spans only when `icon` or `end` is given; they carry no behavior a consumer reaches, and inside a group addons replace them.

good.title: Controlled field with a unit suffix
Invalid field, the group draws the error border

bad.title: Icon passed through Input's slot instead of an addon
bad.why: The slot wraps the field in a span that takes a full row of the group, so the trailing addon no longer shares the field's line. Put the icon in a leading InputGroupAddon.
